source_verification.basis: Lexxion AIRe publisher entry verifies the DOI, title, report author Lucas Javier Segal and corporate-law/DAO keywords. The journal calls it a country report, not a peer-reviewed research article. Its report full text was not publicly inspectable; a separate author account and UBA research-centre technical note substantiate the underlying bill, not the report’s complete analysis.

aboutness.basis: The author publicly describes Argentina’s bill proposing automated companies and DAOs; the University of Buenos Aires computing institute analysed bill PE-193/26, presented to the Senate in May 2026. This supports the substantive Argentine policy object, although the report text was inaccessible.
aboutness.verified_excerpt: The author says the Argentine company-law bill touches automated companies and DAOs but is narrower on AI than presidential messaging implied (author summary, not journal full text).

topic.label: AI regulation
topic.basis: Publisher keywords explicitly include regulatory innovation, algorithmic governance, automated companies and corporate-law reform in Argentina.

futures.mechanism: Company-law proposals governing AI-mediated corporate organization, investment and organizational forms.
futures.why_could_matter: If such provisions become law and are implemented, they could change domestic experiments with AI-based organizations and related regulatory research.
futures.uncertainty: The legislation was still a proposal in cited primary material; publication full text and detailed legal interpretation remain unchecked. No evidence of enactment or impacts is established.
futures.research_question: Would Argentina’s proposed automated-company provisions alter university-industry experiments with AI-mediated business structures if enacted?

results.decision_basis: REVIEW: genuine publisher identity and credible policy object, but the full report is paywalled and the publication’s analysis could not be independently inspected.

source_verification.basis: Intellect’s journal record verifies author Nivea Heluey, DOI 10.1386/jdmp_00173_1, volume 16, pages 195-218 and 31 May 2025 publication. Accessible publisher abstract describes SWOT analysis of UAE policy documents and expert Delphi research. Full article access was restricted; findings below are attributed to the author, not independently replicated.

aboutness.basis: The study’s research object is the United Arab Emirates’ deepfake/AI governance, legal framework and digital media environment, not the journal or author affiliation.
aboutness.verified_excerpt: Publisher abstract describes assessment of UAE deepfake governance using policy-document review and expert Delphi input, reporting gaps in transparency, accountability and privacy.

topic.label: AI regulation
topic.basis: The journal abstract directly investigates UAE AI ethics, deepfake regulation, media trust and regulatory safeguards.

futures.mechanism: Deepfake governance and media-AI testing, auditing and responsible deployment standards.
futures.why_could_matter: If identified transparency and accountability gaps are addressed, that could shape applied research and validation standards for synthetic-media systems in UAE media organizations.
futures.uncertainty: The publisher abstract does not establish the effectiveness of any reforms, the representativeness of the Delphi panel, or later regulatory changes.
futures.research_question: Which governance safeguards would measurably improve transparency and evaluation of deepfake-detection tools in UAE media?

results.decision_basis: KEEP: source, UAE research object and AI regulation connection verified through substantive publisher material; outcomes remain conditional.

source_verification.basis: Publisher-hosted open PDF confirms title, author, DOI and qualitative review of 21 curricula; direct methods section lists Iceland. Country names are named in the sample, but the reported frequencies and conclusions are aggregated and Iceland-specific coding is absent.

aboutness.basis: Iceland’s science curriculum was one of 21 documents collected, but results are pooled across all jurisdictions, so no substantive Iceland-specific AI curriculum finding can be confirmed.
aboutness.verified_excerpt: Methods list Iceland among 21 national curricula; findings report aggregate AI-related coding frequencies without disaggregating Iceland.

topic.label: Artificial intelligence
topic.basis: Artificial intelligence learning, skills, literacy and curricula are the study’s central subject.

futures.mechanism: School science-curriculum content, teacher preparation and the longer-term AI skills pipeline.
futures.why_could_matter: If Iceland’s curriculum is separately assessed and AI-related components are confirmed, it could inform research into future AI literacy and talent development.
futures.uncertainty: Country-specific results are absent; findings cannot be assigned to Iceland from the pooled sample, and future research capacity is not measured.
futures.research_question: What AI competencies are explicitly present in Iceland’s current science curricula, compared with what the cross-national paper counted?

results.decision_basis: REVIEW: Iceland is a studied curriculum in the sample, but the paper supplies no country-level finding suitable for an Iceland-specific verified item.

source_verification.basis: University of Johannesburg repository and indexing label the same DOI 10.59671/zCWcx as an Interciencia article, while its hosted PDF names INFORMATICA, 36(5), ISSN 0868-4952. The authentic journals are separately published at interciencia.net and informatica.vu.lt; a scholarly analysis documents hijacked content attributed to Interciencia. This particular paper’s chain of publication cannot be authenticated; no fraud by the author is asserted.

aboutness.basis: The available abstract discusses industrial policies, minerals, research capabilities and production opportunities in the African automotive battery value chain.
aboutness.verified_excerpt: Repository abstract says African economies could use battery-mineral resources if supported by industrial policy, R&D, partnerships and investment; this claim is not accepted as verified research.

topic.label: Batteries
topic.basis: The work directly addresses Africa’s possible electric-vehicle battery industry.

futures.mechanism: Battery materials research, industrial R&D, processing capacity and automotive supply-chain partnerships.
futures.why_could_matter: If independently supported industrial research partnerships and processing capability were established, local battery value chains could be studied.
futures.uncertainty: Publisher identity conflicts, journal-hijacking risk and lack of an authentic version prevent acceptance of the study’s evidence.
futures.research_question: What independently verified research and processing capacities would be necessary for African battery-manufacturing initiatives?

results.decision_basis: DROP: publication-identity mismatch and credible journal-hijacking concern fail the integrity gate; repository indexing is not corroboration.

source_verification.basis: Open-access Springer Nature Discover Sustainability article verifies DOI, title and 30 May 2025 publication. Its full text describes a Web of Science bibliometric dataset of 687 papers from 2015-2024, research organizations, thematic mapping and Brazil–Africa scientific collaboration. Quantitative findings are those of the study, not independent replication.

aboutness.basis: Brazilian institutions, authors, low-carbon agriculture research output, and Brazil–Africa collaborative knowledge-transfer patterns are principal analyzed objects.
aboutness.verified_excerpt: Article’s results identify Brazil as 22.4% of the 687-document sample and discuss University of São Paulo, Federal University of Viçosa and EMBRAPA in collaborative research mapping.

topic.label: Bibliometrics
topic.basis: A systematic and bibliometric analysis of research trends is explicitly the paper’s method and main aim.

futures.mechanism: Agricultural research collaborations, publication networks, low-carbon farming knowledge transfer and science mapping.
futures.why_could_matter: If documented research networks deepen, they could help identify partners and knowledge gaps for low-carbon agricultural experiments and science collaboration.
futures.uncertainty: Bibliometric frequency does not prove farm-level climate or food-security benefits; results depend on database coverage and search design.
futures.research_question: Which Brazil–Africa research networks are generating reproducible field evidence on low-carbon agriculture rather than publication growth alone?

results.decision_basis: KEEP: authenticated open research and substantive Brazil-focused bibliometric evidence.

source_verification.basis: Open-access Springer book chapter verifies DOI, chapter title, authors and healthcare-in-UAE collection. Its methods use Web of Science/InCites to assess medical and health-science research associated with UAE entities over 2000-2022; chapter first appeared online 2 November 2025.

aboutness.basis: UAE university and healthcare research organizations, their publication records and international collaborations are quantitatively examined.
aboutness.verified_excerpt: Chapter reports 18-fold growth in UAE medical and health research output over 2000-2022 and approximately half of recent publications in international collaboration.

topic.label: Bibliometrics
topic.basis: Bibliometric indicators, research productivity, citations and collaborating institutions are the core research objects.

futures.mechanism: Health-sciences research institutions, biomedical publication infrastructure and international research partnerships.
futures.why_could_matter: If observed collaboration patterns are sustained, they could inform policies for clinical research capacity, infrastructure and research partnerships.
futures.uncertainty: Data end in 2022 and do not establish research quality gains, clinical outcomes, causation or current institutional conditions.
futures.research_question: Which UAE health-science partnerships are producing durable clinical research capacity after the 2022 bibliometric observation window?

results.decision_basis: KEEP: authoritative primary chapter, clear bibliometric topic and UAE-centered institutional evidence.

source_verification.basis: Wiley Geological Journal publisher record verifies author, DOI, online publication on 18 August 2025 and volume 61(6) pages 1683-1695. Accessible primary abstract describes US series 2013Q1-2024Q4 and wavelet-quantile statistical analysis. Full text was not publicly available and no independent ecological replication was located.

aboutness.basis: The quantitative research object is US biodiversity indicators analyzed against domestic AI investment, energy use, GDP and policy uncertainty, not the author location or journal country.
aboutness.verified_excerpt: Wiley abstract says the study models US biodiversity against investment in AI, policy uncertainty, renewable energy and GDP for 2013Q1–2024Q4.

topic.label: Biodiversity
topic.basis: Biodiversity is a named dependent outcome and the declared focus of the study.

futures.mechanism: Ecological indicators and biodiversity monitoring linked to AI-investment and economic-policy research.
futures.why_could_matter: If the reported associations survive independent replication and better biodiversity measurement, they could motivate research into environmental safeguards for AI and energy infrastructure.
futures.uncertainty: The accessible abstract does not explain the biodiversity proxy or establish causal ecological impacts; the claimed statistical associations require replication.
futures.research_question: Can independent US ecological observations validate any biodiversity association with AI investment after controlling for land use and habitat change?

results.decision_basis: KEEP: genuine Wiley article with a substantive US biodiversity study; statistical claims are clearly qualified as unreplicated associations.

source_verification.basis: A complete article-style text is available through an Academia.edu account styling itself as COOU Journal of Arts and Humanities. It identifies author Oyana Isioma Frances, issue 6(1) July 2026 and DOI 10.66837/cjah01/61/01, but no separately authenticated publisher-controlled journal record or resolving DOI landing page was established. Self-upload and assertion of peer review are not external verification.

aboutness.basis: The essay explicitly develops a pan-African philosophical framework for indigenous knowledge, traditional medicine and technological ethics; Africa is its substantive conceptual object rather than an affiliation.
aboutness.verified_excerpt: Uploaded text argues that applying AI and biotechnology to African indigenous knowledge raises problems of contextual interpretation, communal ethics and appropriation.

topic.label: Biotechnology
topic.basis: Biotechnology and traditional medical knowledge are recurring concerns, though the analysis is conceptual rather than a biotechnology experiment or industry study.

futures.mechanism: Indigenous-knowledge governance, research ethics, traditional-medicine knowledge infrastructures and biotechnology consent/benefit-sharing.
futures.why_could_matter: If institutional provenance and argument quality are confirmed, the ethical framework could motivate community-governed knowledge research and safeguards in biotechnology.
futures.uncertainty: The publisher and DOI were not independently authenticated, peer-review process is unclear and no empirical biotechnology outcomes are shown.
futures.research_question: How could community-led consent and benefit-sharing standards be evaluated in African traditional-medicine and biotechnology data projects?

results.decision_basis: REVIEW: genuine accessible text with relevant conceptual content, but scholarly source identity and integrity remain unresolved.

source_verification.basis: Journal of Information Systems and Informatics publisher page and accessible article PDF verify Khadija Sharmin, DOI 10.51519/journalisi.v7i3.1154, September 2025 issue and use of Scopus/R/VOSviewer. It includes a methodological-limits section citing single-database and citation/affiliation biases.

aboutness.basis: The observed corpus is research from Bangladeshi educational institutions, with publication counts, research areas and institution-level contributors.
aboutness.verified_excerpt: Publisher abstract reports Bangladesh-linked cybersecurity publications rising from 23 in 2020 to 77 in 2024, with network security and AI-related cybersecurity among mapped research topics.

topic.label: Cybersecurity
topic.basis: Cybersecurity research output and the Bangladeshi science base form the paper’s central bibliometric dataset.

futures.mechanism: Cybersecurity research capabilities, educational institutions, research collaboration and expertise development.
futures.why_could_matter: If the reported research growth reflects sustained expertise and collaboration, it could help identify gaps in Bangladesh’s cybersecurity skills and applied research infrastructure.
futures.uncertainty: Scopus-only selection, affiliation ambiguity, citation bias and lack of outcome measures limit conclusions about real cybersecurity resilience; future publication growth estimates are not observed results.
futures.research_question: Which Bangladesh cybersecurity research clusters produce independently evaluated tools or sustained university-industry partnerships?

results.decision_basis: KEEP: authenticated Bangladesh-specific cybersecurity research mapping, with explicit database and outcome limitations.

source_verification.basis: Science, Engineering and Health Studies publisher record verifies DOI, authors and 26 December 2025 publication. Accessible abstract gives the design: ISO/IEC 27001:2013, Thailand PDPA and Computer-related Crime Act, validation by 10 experts, 26 controls, and a prototype tested in three organizations.

aboutness.basis: The compliance tool is specifically designed for Thai legislation and tested in organizations operating in Thailand.
aboutness.verified_excerpt: Publisher abstract describes M-SES as a Thai PDPA/cyber-law compliance self-assessment prototype with 26 controls and a three-organization pilot.

topic.label: Cybersecurity
topic.basis: Cybersecurity controls, organizational compliance and assessment technology are the work’s direct focus.

futures.mechanism: Cybersecurity compliance-assessment methods, institutional skills and organizational security measurement.
futures.why_could_matter: If validated at scale, hybrid website-scraping and self-assessment methods could inform safer regulatory compliance testing for Thai organizations.
futures.uncertainty: Only three pilot organizations were tested; the study did not establish a reduction in actual attacks, and website scraping may incompletely capture internal controls.
futures.research_question: How accurately does M-SES predict independently audited cybersecurity controls across diverse Thai organizations?

results.decision_basis: KEEP: source identity, Thai legal and organizational focus and cybersecurity prototype evidence verified, with no invented attack-prevention efficacy.

source_verification.basis: Cambridge University Press open article and PDF verify DOI, authors, accepted January 2026, and 2026 publication. Methods identify 323 Rwandan households across 16 communities and 260 Senegalese households; offers concern solar kits in Rwanda and cookstoves in Senegal. Data were collected in 2015, making current extrapolation especially uncertain.

aboutness.basis: Rwanda is a direct field-study site, including observed actual-purchase offers for three solar-kit sizes and measures of rural households’ willingness to pay.
aboutness.verified_excerpt: Cambridge full text reports data from 323 households in 16 Rwandan communities, with solar-kit purchases examined alongside risk attitudes, affordability and payment flexibility.

topic.label: Energy technology
topic.basis: Technology adoption, off-grid solar systems and behavioural constraints are the central study objects.

futures.mechanism: Off-grid solar research, household adoption evidence, consumer financing and field-tested energy-access programs.
futures.why_could_matter: If updated trials confirm which barriers matter, rural energy innovators could design affordability and information experiments tailored to Rwandan households.
futures.uncertainty: Field data date to 2015, behavioral associations were generally moderate, and local prices, infrastructure and preferences may have changed substantially.
futures.research_question: Do modern Rwandan household trials find that payment flexibility improves off-grid solar adoption more than behavioural nudges?

results.decision_basis: KEEP: independent peer-reviewed empirical evidence directly from Rwanda; the long gap between data collection and publication is clearly disclosed.

source_verification.basis: RSIS publisher page verifies DOI, author names, Bangladesh-centered title and actual publication 3 August 2026 (manifest records a generic 1 January 2026). Only the abstract and bibliography were accessible; advertised PDF fetch failed. The publisher reports only five days between submission and acceptance, a quality-control concern but not proof of wrongdoing.

aboutness.basis: The article concerns Bangladesh’s legal framework governing AI, judicial administration, data protection and cybersecurity.
aboutness.verified_excerpt: The publisher abstract lists intellectual-property rules as one of several legal areas considered, but the stated findings and recommendations are about broad AI governance, accountability, bias, privacy and judicial capacity.

topic.label: Intellectual property
topic.basis: Intellectual property appears as a passing category in the publisher abstract and in references, but is not a demonstrated primary subject, analysis outcome or research-innovation mechanism for this manifest focus issue.

futures.mechanism: Potential IP ownership, authorship and inventorship questions for AI-generated works, not established as a central finding of this paper.
futures.why_could_matter: A separate Bangladesh-focused intellectual-property study could examine R&I implications of AI authorship and patent rules; this article does not substantiate that specific connection.
futures.uncertainty: Full text was unavailable and the abstract did not establish meaningful IP-specific results; article’s editorial scrutiny is not independently established.
futures.research_question: What legal and empirical evidence would demonstrate that AI inventorship or authorship rules affect research commercialization in Bangladesh?

results.decision_basis: DROP: subject is principally AI governance, with only incidental mention of intellectual property; insufficient verified focus-topic relevance.
